convention: Fisher excess kurtosis (normal -> 0); bias=True (population moments E[(x-mu)^4]/E[(x-mu)^2]^2 - 3, NO n-based sample-size correction) -- scipy.stats.kurtosis DEFAULT
blme_kernel: _activation_kurtosis_stats(A, threshold) -> per-channel excess kurtosis over the token axis (axis=0), plus mean/max/frac_above_threshold/tensor_kurtosis summaries

paper.primary: Akhondzadeh, Bojchevski, Eleftheriou, Dazzi, 'KurTail: Kurtosis-based LLM Quantization', Findings of EMNLP 2025, arXiv:2503.01483 (ACL Anthology 2025.findings-emnlp.943)
motivation: Sun et al. 2024, 'Massive Activations in Large Language Models', arXiv:2402.17762

parity_array.composition: cols 0-5 student-t(df=5); 6-11 laplace(0,1); 12-17 uniform(-1,1); 18-23 standard normal

bias_flag_check.note: BLME matches scipy bias=True bit-exactly and is clearly distinguishable from bias=False on small N.

anchors.note: Single-channel large-N (N=400000, default_rng(2024)); recovered value AND exact scipy agreement.

notes: BLME per-channel excess kurtosis reproduces scipy.stats.kurtosis(axis=0, fisher=True, bias=True) to 0.0 (bit-exact) on synthetic activations; anchors recover the textbook kurtoses (Gaussian ~0, Laplace ~3, uniform ~-1.2) and a single-spike channel is very high; all agree with scipy element-for-element. Zero-variance channels are guarded (NaN, dropped from summaries).
